admin.config.feedWarning: Anyone who has this link can see customer names and contact details. Do not share it. Your calendar app keeps a copy of the bookings.

admin.config.venueGeoHint: Position in decimal degrees (WGS-84, as in Google Maps or OpenStreetMap: right-click the entrance and copy the numbers) and/or a plus code (shown in Google Maps). Without a website, the booking site address is used.
admin.config.venueIntro: How customers reach the venue. The approval email can carry these details as a contact card (contact.vcf) that phones and mail apps save with one tap, and the calendar file gets the address and position.

admin.google.intro: Connect your Google Calendar with OAuth to enable synchronization.

admin.google.title: Google Calendar setup
admin.guide.intro: How to create a Google Cloud project, get OAuth credentials and find your Calendar ID.
admin.guide.part1.intro: Register an OAuth app in the Google Cloud Console so the calendar can be synced securely.
admin.guide.part1.step1.text: Sign in with your Google account at
admin.guide.part1.step1.title: Open the Google Cloud Console
admin.guide.part1.step2.text: Open the project list at the top, choose New Project, give it a name (for example Book Me Calendar) and create it.
admin.guide.part1.step2.title: Create or select a project
admin.guide.part1.step3.text: Go to APIs & Services > Library, search for Google Calendar API and click Enable.
admin.guide.part1.step3.title: Enable the Google Calendar API
admin.guide.part1.step4.text: Go to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen, choose External (or Internal with Google Workspace), enter the app name and support email, and save.
admin.guide.part1.step4.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen
admin.guide.part1.step5.text: Go to Credentials > Create Credentials > OAuth client ID, choose Web application and add the redirect URI shown below.
admin.guide.part1.step5.title: Create an OAuth client ID
admin.guide.part1.step6.text: Google then shows the client ID and client secret. Enter both in step 1 of the setup wizard.
admin.guide.part1.step6.title: Copy the credentials
admin.guide.part1.title: Part 1: Client ID and client secret
admin.guide.part2.intro: The Calendar ID decides which calendar the bookings are written to.
admin.guide.part2.note: For your main calendar the ID is your email address or primary. Other calendars have a long ID ending in @group.calendar.google.com.
admin.guide.part2.step1.title: Open Google Calendar
admin.guide.part2.step2.text: Under My calendars, open the menu (three dots) next to the calendar and choose Settings and sharing.
admin.guide.part2.step2.title: Open the calendar settings
admin.guide.part2.step3.text: Scroll down to Integrate calendar and copy the Calendar ID field.
admin.guide.part2.step3.title: Copy the Calendar ID
admin.guide.part2.title: Part 2: Find your Calendar ID
admin.guide.title: Google Calendar setup guide

privacy.intro: This page explains how {business} handles the personal data you give when you book a time.
privacy.purpose.body: Only to handle your booking: to confirm or decline it, to remind you before the appointment and to contact you about changes. The legal basis is the agreement you make when you book (GDPR article 6.1 b).
privacy.purpose.heading: Why

privacy.rights.body: You can ask to see the data we have about you, to have it corrected or deleted, or object to how it is used. Contact us as above. You can also complain to the data protection authority (in Sweden: IMY, imy.se).
privacy.rights.heading: Your rights
privacy.security.body: To protect the booking against spam and attacks, the IP address of blocked or suspicious requests is kept for a limited time in a security log (legitimate interest, GDPR article 6.1 f).
privacy.security.heading: Protection against abuse
privacy.sharing.body: Only the people who handle bookings. The data is stored on our server and is not sold or shared with anyone else. Booking emails are sent through our email provider.
